input.scope: Review-only inspection of two blinded child-facing evaluation candidates (Candidate A design=8548c0a3…acde, Candidate B design=28e4a3e5…f44e) derived from immutable academic contract 274c49ed00318c3c5e7eb4fae53bfbbea61645b4488f4b88780ba9cb431b7361. Observations limited to the provided 1365×768 entry-screen screenshots and blinded machine diagnostics. No candidate modification, selection, preference inference, mastery inference, or aesthetic judgment performed.

firstRequiredAction.observation: A prominent labeled button 'Open the workshop' is visible near screen center-bottom and is plausibly the first required action; the narrative text above explains the task frame (check crates, file reports). A secondary control 'Show the words bigger' is adjacent.

layoutAt1365x768.observation: documentWidth/Height equal viewport (1365×768); no visible clipping, overlap, occlusion, or off-screen content in the entry screenshot. Text is high-contrast and legible at rendered sizes.
layoutAt1365x768.evidence: Candidate A screenshot; diagnostics documentWidth=1365, documentHeight=768

controlResponsiveness.observation: Cannot be confirmed from a static screenshot. Both visible controls have conventional button affordances (border, fill, label). No console or page errors reported that would indicate broken handlers.

uncertainResponsePath.observation: On-screen text explicitly states an uncertain response is legitimate and continuable: 'If a crate puzzles you, mark it Needs another look. That is a real inspector's answer.' Also states no per-item correctness feedback ('no crate will tell you if you were right'), consistent with deferred/withheld feedback and continuation after incorrect responses.
uncertainResponsePath.evidence: Candidate A screenshot text; diagnostics visibleText
uncertainResponsePath.confidence: high for stated intent; medium that the runtime honors it (not exercised)

mathematicsControlsInteraction.observation: Not observable from the entry screen. No mathematics content is visible yet; whether contract mathematics gates progression cannot be confirmed.

confoundRisks.observation: Entry screen carries a moderately long multi-sentence narrative (~60 words) that a child must read before the first action; reading load could confound measurement for weaker readers. Mitigation present: an explicit 'Show the words bigger' control. Interface discovery burden appears low (two clearly labeled buttons).

evidenceClassificationPreservation.observation: Not observable — no event stream was provided. The visible 'Needs another look' affordance suggests an ambiguous/uncertain evidence class is representable, and the no-immediate-feedback framing is compatible with independent-evidence preservation, but emitted event taxonomy (independent/assisted/exposed/ambiguous/friction) cannot be verified without event logs.

contractMutation.observation: No visible content contradicts or alters the academic contract; however, the contract text itself was not supplied, so conformance cannot be verified. Note: the briefing lists candidate design hashes as 'injected_after_frozen_architect_call' while actual hashes are supplied separately — a provenance inconsistency worth recording, not evidence of contract mutation by the candidate.
contractMutation.evidence: Provided hash fields; Candidate A screenshot

firstRequiredAction.observation: A large high-contrast 'Begin' button is centered below a two-line instruction; it is the most salient control and plausibly the first required action. A 'Stop for tonight' control sits top-right. A left rail shows four lamp icons (top one highlighted) that resemble progress indicators; it is not visually clear whether the rail items are interactive, which is a minor discoverability ambiguity.
firstRequiredAction.evidence: Candidate B screenshot; diagnostics visibleControlCount=2 (suggests rail items are non-interactive at this stage)
firstRequiredAction.confidence: high for Begin; medium for rail ambiguity

layoutAt1365x768.observation: documentWidth/Height equal viewport (1365×768); no clipping, overlap, or off-screen content observed. The 'the tower' label at bottom-left is small and low-contrast (dim gray on dark blue) — legible in the screenshot but marginal; potential legibility concern for children or lower-quality displays.
layoutAt1365x768.evidence: Candidate B screenshot; diagnostics documentWidth=1365, documentHeight=768
layoutAt1365x768.confidence: high for layout; medium for the low-contrast label concern

controlResponsiveness.observation: Cannot be confirmed from a static screenshot. 'Begin' and 'Stop for tonight' have button affordances. No console or page errors reported.

uncertainResponsePath.observation: No visible affordance or language on the entry screen indicating an uncertain/'not sure' response path. The line 'What you send is what they keep' implies responses are recorded without immediate correction (consistent with continuation after an incorrect response), but an explicit uncertainty option is not observable at this stage.
uncertainResponsePath.evidence: Candidate B screenshot text; diagnostics visibleText
uncertainResponsePath.confidence: medium — entry screen only; downstream screens not observed

mathematicsControlsInteraction.observation: Not observable from the entry screen; no mathematics content visible. Cannot confirm whether contract mathematics governs progression.

confoundRisks.observation: Reading load on entry is low (two short sentences plus 'Begin'), reducing reading confound relative to text-heavy intros. Potential interface-discovery confound: the left lamp rail's purpose (progress vs. navigation) is unlabeled, and the metaphorical instruction ('What you send is what they keep') may be abstract for younger children. No text-size / accessibility control is visible on this screen.

evidenceClassificationPreservation.observation: Not observable — no event stream provided. 'What you send is what they keep' is consistent with recording raw responses (supports independent evidence), but preservation of assisted/exposed/ambiguous/friction classes cannot be verified without event logs. Absence of a visible uncertainty affordance leaves ambiguous-evidence capture unverified.

contractMutation.observation: No visible content contradicts or alters the academic contract; contract text not supplied so conformance cannot be verified. Same provenance note applies: briefing design-hash fields read 'injected_after_frozen_architect_call' and differ from the actual blinded hashes supplied.
contractMutation.evidence: Provided hash fields; Candidate B screenshot

limitations: Only one static entry-screen screenshot per candidate was provided; task screens containing the contract mathematics were not observed, so mathematics-controls-interaction, control responsiveness, state-change comprehensibility, and error/uncertainty continuation could not be exercised or verified.
No event logs were supplied; preservation of independent/assisted/exposed/ambiguous/friction evidence classification is unverifiable from available artifacts.
The academic contract text corresponding to hash 274c49ed…7361 was not provided; contract-mutation checks are limited to noting the absence of visible contradictions.

Provenance inconsistency in the briefing: 'Candidate design hashes: injected_after_frozen_architect_call' placeholder values differ from the actual blinded candidate hashes listed; this should be reconciled by the process owner. It is recorded as an observation only.
Diagnostics report visibleControlCount=2 for each candidate at entry, consistent with screenshots, but hover/focus states, keyboard operability, and audio/narration support could not be assessed.
Per instructions, no candidate was modified or selected, no child preference or mastery was inferred, and no aesthetic criteria were applied.
